title: Israeli Strike Near Deir al-Balah Bakery Kills 3-Year-Old Tayyem Hamdan and One Other
detail: On Sunday, August 30, 2026, an Israeli airstrike near a bakery in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza killed two Palestinians, according to Gaza health officials: Hussam Nusair, an adult man, and Tayyem Hamdan, a 3-year-old boy. Several others were wounded in the strike. The Israeli military said it had targeted and killed a Hamas militant, alleging Nusair had 'advanced attacks' against Israeli forces and civilians, without addressing the child's death. The strike was the latest in a near-daily pattern of Israeli fire in Gaza despite the October 2025 ceasefire, which Gaza officials say has left more than 1,300 Palestinians dead since it took effect.

confidenceReason: Casualty count and identities confirmed by Gaza health officials and corroborated by Al Jazeera, Al-Monitor and AP wire reporting via U.S. News; IDF confirmed a strike occurred and claimed a militant target but did not dispute the child's death.

title: Israeli Forces Shoot Four Palestinians While Accompanying Settler Attack on Al-Mughayyir
detail: On Sunday, August 30, 2026, Israeli settlers entered the West Bank village of al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah, and attacked residents' vehicles and homes. When Palestinians confronted the attackers, Israeli soldiers accompanying the settlers fired live ammunition and tear gas at the residents. The Palestine Red Crescent Society said its medics treated four young Palestinian men wounded by live fire — two shot in the thigh, one in the chest and one in the abdomen — and evacuated them to hospital; several others were treated for tear-gas inhalation and rubber-coated bullet wounds. Village council head Amin Abu Aliya said Israeli forces were 'restricting access to the village and its surrounding area to Israeli settlers only' during the attack. The incident came a day after Prime Minister Netanyahu condemned settler violence in Qusra and Jalud, underscoring the gap between his statement and events on the ground.

confidenceReason: Casualty figures confirmed by the Palestine Red Crescent Society and corroborated by both Arab News (citing WAFA) and Middle East Eye's live-blog reporting citing the village council head; IDF has not disputed that its forces fired live ammunition.
